newsitem.title: USA: Budget talks atmosphere "very positive" - Sperling.
newsitem.headline: Budget talks atmosphere "very positive" - Sperling.

text.p: Top White House economic aide Gene Sperling said on Monday the atmosphere in budget talks with congressional Republicans was "very positive" and he was "cautiously optimistic" on the chances of a deal.
Sperling, briefing reporters on an unrelated agreement to end sweatshops in the garment industry, also said that both sides in the budget discussions would have to "give a little."

"As (House Budget Committee Chairman John) Kasich said yesterday, I think there is a sense of goodwill and good faith in the room, and probably far better than we had in 1995 and 1996," Sperling said. "There is an explicit understanding of all of us that all of us are going to have to give a little, but give in a way that still protects our values," he added.

"There's an atmosphere and an attitude that is very positive," he said. "I think that it is very possible to get an agreement, and I, as (Office of Management and Budget Director) Frank Raines said, would be cautiously optimistic."

Asked about a statement earlier on Monday by Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, that this was the "make-it-or-break-it week" in the talks, Sperling replied, "He's been trying to make all sides move forward expeditiously and I think it's right for him to keep that pressure up.

"But whether it's exactly this week or next week, I think his main point is that we need to move quickly, that we have an opportunity right now over the next couple of weeks to have at least a chance, or a significant chance, of getting an early deal," he added.
"That would be a pretty significant thing and I think we should do everything we can to make sure we don't waste that opportunity," he added.
